title: FastStrap: Client Onramp Pocket Playbook
body:
Purpose
This is a compact "pocket" playbook for product teams, solutions engineers, and internal SDK authors to run a reliable fast-path onboarding flow: 10 minutes from checkout to a validated first request, then a 30-minute mini-workshop to exercise fallbacks and telemetry. 

Audience and constraints
- Primary: software engineers trying Redwood API for the first time (web/mobile backend).
- Secondary: SEs running demos, solutions engineers doing POCs.
- Constraint: minimal friction; assume user has Node >=16 or Python 3.10 installed.

High-level goals (non-exhaustive)
- Make first request predictable: success, cost telemetry, latency sample.
- Provide copy-paste examples for JS/Python/cURL.
- Surface common failure modes and quick recovery commands.
- Offer a short 30-minute workshop itinerary for demos and internal training.

What “first success” looks like
- Valid API key configured and used by a small sample app.
- One text-generation request completed (streaming optional) and returned with token counts.
- Telemetry shows one request on console: route, model, duration, tokens.
- Minimal CI smoke test (assert response status, token usage < threshold).

Quickstart snippets (copy-paste)
1) cURL (quickest)
   curl -sS -X POST https://api.redwood-inference.ai/v1/generate \
     -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" \
     -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
     -d '{"model":"rwd-compat-3b","input":"Write a 3-line launch checklist for our demo"}'

2) Node (official lightweight example)
   // index.js\   import fetch from 'node-fetch'
   const res = await fetch('https://api.redwood-inference.ai/v1/generate', {
     method: 'POST',
     headers: { 'Authorization': `Bearer ${process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY}`, 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
     body: JSON.stringify({ model: 'rwd-compat-3b', input: 'Summarize the meeting notes in 2 bullets' })
   })
   const data = await res.json()
   console.log('text:', data.output[0].content || data.output)

3) Python (requests)
   import os, requests
   url='https://api.redwood-inference.ai/v1/generate'
   r = requests.post(url, json={'model':'rwd-compat-3b','input':'Create a short apology email'}, headers={'Authorization':f"Bearer {os.environ.get('REDWOOD_API_KEY')}", 'Content-Type':'application/json'})
   print(r.json())

Local-sim mode (notes to self)
- For offline demos, use the local-stub harness: run `./devtools/local-stub --seed demo` and point examples to http://localhost:8080.
- Stub returns deterministic output; include a note in the README: "local-stub not for perf telemetry".

Checklist: pre-demo quick triage (2–5 mins)
- Confirm API key has no IP restriction and is non-expired. (Common pitfall: prod key used for demo with CIDR block)
- Check rate-limits on the account; bump quota for enterprise demos.
- If streaming: confirm ws proxy allowed by local firewall.
- If response slow: check region routing header (x-rw-region) and try alternate region.

Smoke test to add to CI (example)
- Step: run a lightweight request to /v1/generate with model rwd-compat-3b.
- Assert: HTTP 200, response contains "output" and token_count < 200
- If fails (401/429/5xx) flag build as unstable and open JIRA with console logs.

Common failure modes & remediation (quick notes)
- 401 Invalid key: user stored key in .env but process not restarted -> remind about export and env reload.
- 429 Rate-limited: suggest backoff with exponential jitter; pre-warm with low-priority warmup requests.
- 5xx transient: check model variant fallback plan; retry once then switch to fallback route (rwd-compat-1b-fallback).
- Malformed JSON 400: often caused by smart quotes from copied docs — include a tiny sanitizer snippet in SDK.

Telemetry and observability to show during demo
- Console quick-check: model, route, token counts (input/output), latency ms.
- Dashboard: show per-route throughput, top prompt templates, and an alert rule sample for token regressions.
- Instrumentation pointers: include a tiny snippet for tracing header propagation (x-rw-trace-id).

Warmup & cost controls (ops-first checklist)
- Recommend a single warmup request per instance before a live demo to populate KV cache.
- For POCs, use quantized model variants to reduce token cost; show side-by-side estimate: rwd-compat-3b ~ $0.0018/req vs rwd-compat-1b-quant ~ $0.0005/req (example).
- Add rate-limiter: client-side token bucket config with a 100 qps cap for sandbox users.

30-minute mini-workshop (internal SEs)
- 0–5 min: orientation — goals, account setup, where to find API key.
- 5–15 min: hands-on — run cURL, Node, Python first requests (pair programming).
- 15–25 min: failure drills — simulate 401, 429, slow response and exercise fallbacks.
- 25–30 min: telemetry demo + checklist to export run logs, token billing sample.

Snippets for SDK maintainers (instrumentation & UX)
- Auto-sanitize helper (JS): trim smart quotes, enforce utf-8, fallback to truncated input when > 2048 tokens.
- Friendly error mapping: map 429 -> Retry-After header and implement exponential backoff with capped jitter. Return a clear user-facing message: "Redwood is busy — retry in a few seconds".
- Telemetry hook: emit minimal telemetry event after first successful request: {model, route, latency_ms, token_in, token_out, demo_flag:true}. Keep events small and sample at 10% for demos.

Unresolved questions (TODOs)
- Should we expose a single-file "demo-key" with limited quota for SEs? Security review needed. (JIRA-SEC-223)
- Decision: standardize on rwd-compat-3b or use small quantized default for free sandbox? (ask Product)
- CLI helper: add `rw-cli demo init` scaffolding (owner: @Nina).

Copy snippets & README placement
- Place these copy-paste snippets in: /quickstarts/faststrap/README.md and add a small GIF showing a successful response in console.

Notes to SEs: quick language for customer emails
- Subject: "Quick Redwood demo — 10 minutes to first response"
- Body: include one liner how-to, three steps: 1) set API key, 2) run cURL snippet, 3) share screenshot and tag eng-devexp.

Appendix: minimal troubleshooting commands
- Check env: `env | grep REDWOOD_API_KEY`
- Ping endpoint: `curl -I https://api.redwood-inference.ai/v1/health`
- View last 24h quota: (linked to console on enterprise accounts)

Small logs template for triage (copy into support ticket)
- Account ID: ____
- Region tried: ____
- Model: ____
- Request timestamp: ____
- HTTP status + body (attach)

Why this is different from big guides
- Intentional: micro, copy-paste-first, engineered for low cognitive load. This file should be the minimal set an SE can hand to a developer and expect a working demo in 10 minutes.

If you use this doc please:
- Add any successful workshop notes to the GH PR linked above.
- If you create a demo-key, add a short security rationale and expiration policy into JIRA-SEC-223.

Last updated: 2025-11-15 by Evan Cho (draft)
